title: sre-weekly-update-2026-07-04
content:
Summary:
- This week focused on two operational incidents (one SEV2, one SEV3), on-call handoffs refinement, and follow-ups from last week's SLO review. No customer-facing data exposures.

Metrics snapshot (last 7d vs SLO targets):
- Hosted API availability (target 99.95%): 99.97% — within target.
- Text-generation P95 latency (target: <= 150ms for cached warm requests): 172ms (regression during SEV2 spike).
- Error budget remaining (monthly window): 68% (after recent incidents).
- Dedicated pool request success rate: 99.88% (slight dip during KV cache incident).

Incidents:
1) SEV2 - Elevated 5xx and P95 latency spike across us-west1 (2026-07-01 03:14–03:50 UTC)
   - Impact: ~12% increase in 5xx for hosted-generation endpoints, P95 latency increased to ~420ms during peak, affecting interactive apps and streaming timeouts.
   - Detection: Alert from latency burn alert (P95 > 200ms sustained for 5m).
   - Root cause (prelim): A routing policy rollout (rollout-id: SRE-342) accidentally favored cold model-variant replicas for a subset of traffic due to a mismatch in the variant compatibility matrix. Cold variants had empty KV caches causing high warm-up latency.
   - Mitigation: Rapid rollback of the routing policy and targeted cache-evict/rewarm for affected nodes. Traffic normalized within ~36 minutes.
   - Postmortem actions:
     * Add automated canary checks for routing policy changes that verify variant cache-warmth and P95 on a small traffic slice (owner: David Kim, due: 2026-07-09).
     * Add a compatibility validation step to the router config pipeline to prevent incompatible variant preference (owner: Samantha Ortiz, due: 2026-07-16).
     * Create runbook step for "routing-policy rollback + selective rewarm" and link into runbooks (owner: Aisha Patel, due: 2026-07-10).
   - Related artifacts: SRE-342 (routing rollout), PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/587, Confluence INC-2026-07-01.

2) SEV3 - KV cache replica lag causing tail latency for Dedicated pools (2026-07-02 11:20–12:05 UTC)
   - Impact: Dedicated customers in eu-west1 experienced increased tail latencies (P99 up ~3x) for ~45 minutes; no SLA breach but customer tickets opened.
   - Detection: Cache lag alarm + customer ticket from dedicated-customer-12.
   - Root cause: Recent autoscaling event triggered rebalancing; rebalancer started moving partitions with a too-low threshold causing transient overload on a small set of replica nodes.
   - Mitigation: Manually increased rebalance-threshold, scaled up cache nodes by +2, and rebalanced slowly.
   - Postmortem actions:
     * Tweak rebalancer thresholds and add gradual throttling to partition moves (owner: Liam Zhang, due: 2026-07-11).
     * Add dedicated-pool health check that correlates cache-lag with tail-latency for earlier detection (owner: SRE team, due: 2026-07-18).

On-call handoffs / notes:
- Outgoing: Priya Menon (2026-07-03 09:00 UTC)
  * Notes: observed noisy neighbor on kube-node-09; placed drain-suspect label. No immediate action required but monitor CPU steal.
- Incoming: Tom Alvarez (2026-07-03 09:00 UTC)
  * Notes: follow up on eks node drain scheduling; responsible for running canary for upcoming routing-policy fix.
- On-call pager rota for next week: Tom Alvarez -> Mei Chen -> Carlos Rivera -> Priya Menon. Ensure all have access to runbook and runbook has recent example of routing rollback.

Operational items / work in progress:
- SLO review follow-up: Weigh increasing P95 latency SLO to 160ms for cold-start sensitive endpoints vs adding stronger cache-warm policies. (owner: Product infra + SRE, due: 2026-07-20)
- Runbook cleanup: Consolidate "model-variant cold-start" steps into a single runbook page; add drill checklist. (owner: Aisha Patel, due: 2026-07-12)
- Observability: Dashboard updates to show "variant cache warmth" and per-variant P95 for top 10 models (owner: Samantha Ortiz, due: 2026-07-15).
- Capacity ask: QA + staging cluster CPU quota needs +30% for next month to support larger canaries (request submitted to infra-quotas).

Upcoming maintenance / planned work:
- 2026-07-10 02:00–04:00 UTC: Kernel + container runtime security patching in eu-west1 Dedicated pool. Expected rolling restarts with 5–10m connection disruption per node. Communications: customer notice scheduled for 2026-07-06.
- 2026-07-12: Canary rollout of routing policy with added checks (see mitigation action). Will run on 1% traffic for 2 hours then ramp to 10% if metrics stable.

Blockers / requests:
- Need infra help to provision +2 cache nodes in eu-west1 earlier than standard lead time (owner: Liam Zhang).
- SRE needs product confirmation on endpoints that are cold-start tolerant vs latency-sensitive to finalize SLO changes.

Action items (short):
- David Kim: Implement canary gating for routing policy (due 2026-07-09).
- Samantha Ortiz: Add variant-warmth metric to observability dashboard (due 2026-07-15).
- Liam Zhang: Tune cache rebalancer thresholds and add throttling (due 2026-07-11).
- Aisha Patel: Draft routing-policy rollback runbook + examples (due 2026-07-10).

Notes / open questions:
- Should we introduce an automated preflight that simulates a small synthetic workload to validate cache-warmth before traffic shift? (proposal: run in staging daily)
- How do we prioritize Dedicated customer tail-latency mitigations versus hosted API P95 improvements? Need product guidance.

Retrospective highlights:
- Detection and mitigation were fast for the SEV2 incident once alerts fired, but rollout validation is a clear gap.
- Communication to CS was adequate for Dedicated customers on KV cache incident, but we should improve templated customer messages for tail-latency events.

If anything else needed (graphs, raw logs), ping me or open SRE-ops slack thread and tag on-call.

Signed-off-by: Aisha Patel (SRE Lead)
